evals.prompt: Use gtm-setup to create a new GTM Context Project for Northstar Compliance. The active person is Jordan Lee, SDR. Use the simple path and skip enrichment links.
evals.expected_output: A valid Northstar Compliance GTM Context Repository under a temp GTM_HOME, a local registry.json outside the repo, an initial commit containing only setup scaffold files, and a setup summary reached within the three-interaction budget.
expectations: Simple-path transcript contains at most three user prompts before the setup summary.
The scaffold checker passes against the generated repo in a temp GTM_HOME.
registry.json matches the ADR 0003 shape and local active state is absent from the org repo.
The generated .gitignore blocks local state, secrets, temporary files, logs, and ephemeral output families.
The initial commit exists and contains only scaffold or confirmed-enrichment files.

evals.prompt: Re-run gtm-setup for the same Northstar Compliance org, repair a missing ignore rule without overwriting human-authored files, and exercise source-assisted enrichment with public, private, local, invite, and tokenized links.
evals.expected_output: A same-org re-run leaves the valid repo untouched except local registry state, repair mode changes only missing scaffold rules, and secret-bearing or tokenized source links are never committed.
expectations: Re-running setup on the same org is idempotent and leaves the existing repo untouched.
Repair mode preserves human-authored files and user-defined ignore rules while adding only missing scaffold rules.
The repair commit is scoped to repair-only changes.
The source-link classifier marks unsafe links as never-commit and committed files/history omit unsafe URLs.
